newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/9.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/9.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 9.0/9.5 percent on Thursday on ample supply, dealers said.
They said the market was quiet, with plenty of rupiah being offered, keeping operators calm as the new bank reserve requirement rate, effective on April 16, edges closer.
"I don't believe there won't be any impact on the market. Some estimate an additional drain of five to eight trillion rupiah to meet the new requirement," one dealer said.
The central bank supplied 267 billion rupiah on Thursday.
Another said banks with good reputations could tap the interbank market after the rate becomes effective, switching focus from deposit funds which are subject to the new rule.
"I think interbank bank rates would then remain well supported because more reputable banks would tap this market rather than look for deposits," he added.
One-month money was at 12.00/12.75 percent and three-month at 13.25 percent.
The central bank offered 6-7 day bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 8.34 percent, compared with 9.43 percent on Monday.
One dealer said a flattening of the long-term yield curve of the rupiah might have some impact on the bond market.
"In two or three days time people who cannot get out from the long-term swap market might hedge through the bond market," the dealer said.
Bond dealers said, however, the market was still quiet. The PLN V/A bonds were still yielding 14.9 percent.
